January 31, 1942.

Ting Sih Shan (丁錫山), Commander of
the Provisionally Organized 13th Division
of the Nanking Army - reported to have
been detained by the Japanese authorities.

It is reported that Ting Sih Shan, Commander
of the Provisionally Organized 13th Division of the
Nanking Army, has been detained in Hongkew by the
Japanese authorities since the middle of January,
1942.

Since joining the Nanking Government, Ting
Sih Shan has been increasing the strength of his
Division. It has now more than 20,000 men, which
figure is far beyond the authorized strength. At
the beginning of January, his Division was transferred
from Shanghai to Kashing, and he made demands for
money and arms which displeased the Nanking authorities.
This may possibly account for his detention by the
Japanese authorities.

The Nanking authorities are reorganizing the
Division and will transfer the surplus men to other
units. When this has been successfully completed
without untoward incidents, it is believed that Ting
Sih Shan will be released.

1942年1月31日。

南京陆军暂编第十三师师长丁锡山——据报已被日本当局拘留。

据报，南京陆军暂编第十三师师长丁锡山自1942年1月中旬以来，一直被日本当局拘留在虹口。

丁锡山自加入南京政府以来，一直在扩充其师的兵力。目前该师人数已超过20,000人，这一数字远远超出编制限额。1月初，他的部队从上海调往嘉兴，他提出的钱款和武器要求令南京当局不满。这可能是他被日本当局拘留的原因。

南京当局正在重组该师，并将多余人员调往其他部队。据信，如果这一过程顺利完成且未发生意外事件，丁锡山将被释放。

Assistance rendered to the Western Shanghai
Area Special police Force

At 11 a.m. on the 4th August 1941 Chief Inspector
Yamaguchi attached to General Affairs Branch of the
W.S.A.S.P. Force called at C.I. offices and requested
assistance of the S.M.police to visit the Fuh Tan Psycho-
logy Experimental Middle School, at 266 Peking Road for
purpose of verifying an identity of a male Chinese named
Lee Hsien (李鑫) believed to be a student of the insti-
tution noted. C.I. Yamaguchi stated that this person was
killed on the 1st August 1941, outside the gate of Jess-
field Park when he made an attempt to throw a hand grenade
into a procession staged in commemoration of the recog-
nition of Wang Ching Wei Regime. The hand grenade had
exploded in the hands of this student killing him instant-
ly on the spot.

Personal papers found on the dead body led to the
identification of this person.

Enquiries conducted by D.I. Soong Ping Tsung, the
undersigned and C.I. Yamaguchi at the Fuh Tan Psychology
Experimental Middle School corroborated the fact of the
killed person being a student of this school. His parti-
culars learned at the school are as follows :

Lee Hsien, age 20, native of Tientsin, S/Student,
resided at 601/607 Rue Lafayette, French Concession.

向西上海地区特别警察队提供协助

1941年8月4日上午11时，西上海地区特别警察队总务科附设的巡官山口（Yamaguchi）造访刑事科办公室，请求上海公共租界警务处协助前往北京路266号的复旦心理实验中学，以核实一名名为李鑫的中国男子的身份，此人据信是该机构的学生。山口巡官称，此人于1941年8月1日在兆丰公园门外试图向庆祝承认汪精卫政权的游行队伍投掷手榴弹时被杀。手榴弹在此学生手中爆炸，致其当场立即死亡。

在尸体上发现的个人文件有助于确认此人的身份。

由督察宋秉宗、签署人及山口巡官在复旦心理实验中学进行的调查证实，死者确系该校学生。在学校获悉的其个人资料如下：

李鑫，20岁，天津籍，学生，居住于法租界霞飞路601/607号。

August 2, 1941.

Celebrations held by local Nanking
Authorities on August 1 in connection
with the recognition of the Nanking
Government by Germany, Italy and six
other nations

On August 1, local organs of the Nanking
Government held celebrations in connection with the
recognition of that government by Germany, Italy and
six other nations. Preparations for the celebrations
were undertaken by the Shanghai Branch of the Social
Movement Direction Committee, 527 Range Road.
Distribution and posting of handbills and
posters of a pro-Japanese, pro-Nazi and anti-Chungking
nature commenced on July 30 in Japanese occupied areas,
the Extra-Settlement Roads Area in the Western District
and also in districts north of Soochow Creek. In the
above mentioned areas, "Pailous" with electric lights
were erected at the entrances of Nanking official
organs and white cloth banners bearing words of
celebration were displayed in principal thoroughfares.
On July 31 and August 1, coloured slips bearing
slogans of a pro-Japanese and anti-Chungking nature
made their appearance in the International Settlement
south of Soochow Creek. Some of the slips were
reported to have been thrown from a certain motor car
proceeding eastward along Bubbling Well and Nanking
Roads from the corner of Bubbling Well and Carter Roads
at about 2 p.m. August 1.
The principal events of the day are briefly
related hereunder:-
(a) Celebration meeting in Chinese Chamber of Commerce
Building, North Soochow Road
Between 9.40 a.m. and 11.10 a.m. August 1, some
page_data.zh:
S.l, 特别处，
1941年8月2日。

当地南京当局于8月1日为庆祝德国、意大利及其他六国承认南京政府而举行的庆祝活动

8月1日，南京政府的地方机构举行了庆祝活动，以纪念德国、意大利及其他六国对该政府的承认。庆祝活动的准备工作由位于兰路527号的社会运动指导委员会上海分会负责。
自7月30日起，在日军占领区、西区越界筑路区以及苏州河以北的地区，开始分发和张贴具有亲日、亲纳粹和反重庆性质的传单和海报。在上述地区，南京官方机构入口处搭建了装有电灯的“牌楼”，主要干道上悬挂着写有庆祝字样的白布横幅。7月31日和8月1日，带有亲日和反重庆口号的彩色纸条出现在苏州河以南的国际租界内。据报道，其中一些纸条是8月1日下午2点左右，从一辆沿静安寺路和南京路向东行驶的汽车上抛下的，该车当时正从静安寺路与卡德路拐角处驶出。
当天的主要活动简述如下：-
(a) 在北苏州路中国商会大楼举行的庆祝集会
8月1日上午9时40分至11时10分之间，约

page_data.en:
- 2 -

250 persons, mostly representatives of official organs
and labour unions affiliated with the Nanking
Government, held a celebration meeting in the Chinese
Chamber of Commerce Building, North Soochow Road.
This function was marked by speeches of a pro-Nazi
and pro-Japanese nature. The attendance, including
4 Japanese gendarmes in plainclothes, dispersed after
taking a group photograph and shouting the following
slogans :-

"Consolidate the Oriental Axis!"
"Establish a New Order in the Orient!"

At 8.35 p.m., some fireworks were set off on
the premises.

(b) Motorcar Procession in Hongkew

At about 10 a.m. August 1, seven hire cars,
decorated with coloured handbills and white cloth
banners, each carrying about two or three persons,
started a procession from outside the Shanghai Branch
of the Social Movement Direction Committee, 527 Range
Road, and returned to the same place about 50 minutes
later where they dispersed after having traversed the
following roads :- Range Road, North Szechuen Road
and Dixwell Road. During the procession, coloured
slips bearing slogans were scattered on the roads.

(c) Lantern Procession in the Extra-Settlement Roads
Area in the Western District

Early in the afternoon of August 1,
representatives from various organizations affiliated
with the Nanking Government began to assemble outside
Jessfield Park and vicinity and at 7 p.m., they and
page_data.zh:
- 2 -

250人，大多是南京政府所属官方机构和工会的代表，在北苏州路中国商会大楼举行了庆祝集会。此次活动的特点是发表了亲纳粹和亲日性质的演讲。包括4名便衣日本宪兵在内的出席者在合影并高呼以下口号后散去：-

“巩固东方轴心！”
“建立东方新秩序！”

晚上8时35分，在该处燃放了一些烟花。

(b) 虹口的汽车游行

8月1日上午10点左右，七辆装饰着彩色传单和白布横幅的租赁汽车，每车载有两三人，从兰路527号社会运动指导委员会上海分会门外出发开始游行，约50分钟后返回原地解散，游行路线经过以下道路：兰路、北四川路和狄思威路。游行期间，道路上散落着印有口号的彩色纸条。

(c) 西区越界筑路区的灯笼游行

8月1日下午早些时候，隶属于南京政府的各组织代表开始在兆丰公园及周边地区集合，晚上7点，他们与其

page_data.en:
- 3 -

others, numbering approximately 8,000 persons, started
a lantern procession which proceeded eastward along
Yu Yuen Road. The procession was headed by three fire
engines, one of which carried a portrait of the late
Dr. Sun Yat-sen, and accompanied by twenty Japanese
gendarmes, ten soldiers of the Nanking Army, and a
number of constables of the Shanghai Western Area
Special Police Force, etc. From Yu Yuen Road, the
procession turned into Edinburgh Road and then along
Brenan, Jessfield and Tifeng Roads, westward along
Yu Yuen Road into Edinburgh Road and returned to
Tifeng Road via Great Western Road. They dispersed
at Tifeng Road at 11 p.m.
(d) Bomb explosion near Jessfield Park
At about 5 p.m. August 1, a handgrenade exploded
near Jessfield Park which resulted in the wounding of
two persons, one fatally.
(e) Situation in Nantao, Chapei and Pootung
Apart from the distribution and posting of
propaganda matter, the occasion was not celebrated
in any other form in the above mentioned districts.
The iron gates between Nantao and the French
Concession were closed throughout the day, August 1,
in consequence of a shooting affray which took place
in Nantao on the night of July 31 and in which one
male Chinese was reported to have been fatally shot
and one Japanese gendarme to have been wounded.
(f) Anti-Nanking Propaganda
On the morning of August 1, slogans of an anti-
Nanking nature were found pasted on electric light
page_data.zh:
- 3 -

他人共计约8,000人，开始了沿愚园路向东行进的灯笼游行。游行队伍由三辆消防车领头，其中一辆载有已故孙中山博士的肖像，并有二十名日本宪兵、十名南京陆军士兵以及若干上海西区特别警察队警员等陪同。队伍从愚园路转入爱丁堡路，然后沿布伦南路、兆丰路和提丰路行进，再沿愚园路向西进入爱丁堡路，最后经大西路返回提丰路。他们于晚上11点在提丰路解散。
(d) 兆丰公园附近的炸弹爆炸
8月1日下午5点左右，兆丰公园附近发生手榴弹爆炸，导致两人受伤，其中一人重伤不治。
(e) 南市、闸北和浦东的情况
除了分发和张贴宣传品外，上述地区没有以其他任何形式庆祝该 occasion。
由于7月31日晚在南市发生了一起枪击事件，导致一名中国男子 reportedly 被枪杀，一名日本宪兵受伤，因此在8月1日全天，南市与法租界之间的铁门一直关闭。
(f) 反南京宣传
8月1日上午，在河南路桥与市场之间的北河南路上，发现电线杆上贴有反南京性质的标语。据报道，张贴者是几名儿童。

page_data.en:
- 4 -

poles on North Honan Road between the Market and the
Honan Road Bridge. It is reported that the posting
was done by some children.

------------------

Propaganda matter of a pro-Nanking nature, which
came into the possession of the Municipal Police,
consisted of posters and coloured slips bearing
slogans which are translated as follows:-

(a) Celebrate the recognition of the National
Government by Germany, Italy and other friendly
nations!

(b) Long live the emancipation of the Nation!

(c) Strengthen the National Government (Nanking)
and accelerate the realisation of national peace!

(d) Long live the Axis Powers!

(e) Exterminate the Chungking Government which relies
upon the Old Order for its existence!

(f) Overthrow Communism!

(g) Smash the Old Order of International Aggression!

(h) Unite the Axis Powers in the Orient and establish
a "World Wide New Order"!

(i) Establish New Order for racial co-existence and
co-prosperity.

Certified true copy.

L. Richardson
CLK/.

- 4 -

---

工部局警务处获得的亲南京性质的宣传品包括海报和印有口号的彩色纸条，翻译如下：-

(a) 庆祝德国、意大利及其他友好国家承认国民政府！

(b) 民族解放万岁！

(c) 加强国民政府（南京），加速实现国家和平！

(d) 轴心国万岁！

(e) 消灭依靠旧秩序生存的重庆政府！

(f) 推翻共产主义！

(g) 粉碎国际侵略的旧秩序！

(h) 联合东方轴心国，建立“世界新秩序”！

(i) 建立种族共存共荣的新秩序。

核证无误副本。

L. Richardson
CLK/.

At about 5 p.m. August 1, a handgrenade exploded

Apart from the distribution and posting of

The iron gates between Nantao and the French

in consequence of a shooting affray which took place
in Nantao on the night of July 31 and in which one
male Chinese was reported to have been fatally shot

deck of a No.1 Route Omnibus along Yu Yuen Road, and

      当时他正乘坐1路公共汽车沿愚园路由东向西行驶，在汽车上层通道上，刚刚驶过位于愚园路北侧、极司非尔公园以东不远处的银马车行（Silver Taxi Garage）后，他听到车行西侧的一块空地上传来一声巨响，向车窗外望去，只见升起一团黑烟，且有数人躺在地上。

Tsang Ching Yuen ( 張慶雲 )
Ningpo                                      Self written
B'well Station      August 1, 1941      translated      Clerk C.F.Ho.
                                        xxxxxxxx

My name is Tsang Ching Yuen, age 20 years, native of
Ningpo, residing No.4 Tsang Yee Faung off Jessfield Road.
I had studied in the Tse Dah Middle School in Tientsin and
graduated there. Then I came to Shanghai and studied in
the Chung Kuo Middle School for 1 year, and now I have pass-
ed the examination in the Shanghai Law Academy.

My father named Tsang Chu Sien used to work in the
Cheng Foo Company situated in the Ching Chang Building,
Kiangse Road but resigned about two months ago.

I heard that there would be a lantern procession at
the Jessfield Park to-day, so with the intention of attend-
ing same I left my home at about 3p.m. and it was about
4p.m. when I arrived at Yu Yuen Road.

As I was walking near the Silver Taxi Garage, I sudden-
ly heard an explosion, I commenced to run towards Brenan
Road and found that I had received certain injuries. I
then called a ricsha and when passing Edinburgh Road near
Kinnear Road I came across a Western Area Special police on
a motor cycle who, after I had explained the affair to him,
told me to attend a Doctor immediately.

I then boarded a M/bus at Edinburgh and Yu Yuen Roads
corner and paid the ricsha coolie $1.00.

I left the Bus at Bubbling Well stop and intended to
engage a M/car from the Johnson Garage (to go to hospital)
when I met a policeman who brought me to B'Well Station
where I was sent to the Red Cross Hospital, Avenue Haig for
treatment.

The above is my true statement.

(Sgd.) Tsang Ching Yuen.

张庆云
宁波                                      亲笔书写
静安寺捕房      1941年8月1日      译者      文书 C. F. 何 (音译)
                                        xxxxxxxx

我名叫张庆云，现年20岁，浙江宁波人，住址为极司非尔路旁张家弄（音译）4号。我曾就读于天津志达中学（音译，Tse Dah Middle School）并毕业。此后我来到上海，在中华中学（Chung Kuo Middle School）学习了1年，目前已通过上海法政学院（Shanghai Law Academy）的入学考试。

我的父亲名叫张聚先（音译，Tsang Chu Sien），曾在江西路金城大厦的承富公司（音译，Cheng Foo Company）工作，但于大约两个月前辞职。

我听说今天极司非尔公园会有提灯巡游，所以想去围观，于下午3时许离开家，大约在下午4时抵达愚园路。

当我走到银马车行附近时，突然听到一声爆炸，我便开始往白利南路方向跑，随后发现自己受了些伤。我于是叫了一辆人力车，当途径爱底巴拉路靠近开纳路（Kinnear Road）时，遇到了一名骑摩托车的沪西特别警察，我向他说明了情况后，他让我立刻去看医生。

随后我在爱底巴拉路和愚园路转角处登上了一辆公共汽车，并付给人力车夫1.00元。

我在静安寺站下了公车，正打算从强生车行（Johnson Garage）租一辆汽车（去医院）时，遇到了一名巡警，他将我带到了静安寺捕房，随后我被送往海格路红十字会医院接受治疗。

以上所述均属实。

（签字）张庆云。

Lantern Procession - August 1.

Mr. Jabin Hsu called on Mr. R.T. Bryan,
Acting Secretary & Commissioner General, and in-
formed him that many persons might be leaving the
Settlement at the Western Barriers tomorrow evening
and he hoped there would be no difficulties at the
Barriers, since there might be some congestion of
traffic.

Mr. Hsu was put through to me on the tele-
phone and I informed him if a few individuals were
going West and there was no demonstration or display
of lanterns the Police were not interested.

On the other hand if large groups were
formed or lanterns were lit or there was any form
of demonstration such groups will be broken up and
offenders might be arrested.

I told him that even the suggestion of
such a situation within Settlement limits at this
period when every effort was being made to put down
terrorism and maintain peace and order was quite out-
rageous.

Please take action of a strong preventative
nature and ask the assistance of the U.S. Fourth
Marines and the Royal Italian Landing Party (St. Marco
Detachment).

It must be understood that small parties
or individuals can pass freely and Police action will

徐嘉彬（Jabin Hsu）先生拜访了代理秘书兼总办 R.T. Bryan 先生，并告知他明晚可能有许多人离开租界前往西部边界，他希望边界处不要出现困难，因为可能会出现交通拥堵。

徐先生通过电话与我联系，我告诉他，如果只是少数个人向西行进，且没有示威或展示灯笼的行为，警方不会介入。

另一方面，如果形成大型团体、点燃灯笼或有任何形式的示威，这些团体将被驱散，违法者可能会被逮捕。

我告诉他，在当前全力镇压恐怖主义、维持和平与秩序的时期，甚至在租界范围内提出此类情况的建议都是极其荒谬的。

The motorcars will first assemble at Hongkew Park

occupied areas on July 30. A "Pailou" is being
erected at the entrance of the Chinese Chamber of
Commerce Building and white cloth banners bearing
words of celebration have been displayed at the north

Celebration of the Recognition of the Nanking Government
by Germany, Italy and other pro-Axis nations

Further to the report dated July 26, a function
will be held locally on August 1, under the auspices of
the Shanghai Branch of the Social Movement Direction
Committee, in celebration of the recognition of the
Nanking Government by Germany, Italy and six other pro-Axis
nations.

A circular notice has been issued by the Shanghai
Municipality Labour Union Readjustment Committee to the
effect that a meeting in celebration of the event will be
held at 9 a.m. August 1 in the premises of the Chamber of
Commerce on North Soochow Road, and instructing the various
labour unions in this locality to detail representatives,
who are to be issued with identification papers, to attend
the meeting. The proposed assembly near the Jessfield
Park at about 6 p.m. August 1, is not changed.

According to information secured by pro-Nanking
Government quarters, a party of some fifteen special service
men connected with the Chungking Government will be
despatched here to create trouble in connection with the
proposed celebration.

S.1, Special Branch.
July 23, 1941.

Lantern procession in celebration of
the recognition of the National
Government (Nanking) by Germany and
other Axis Powers to be held on July 28
in the Western District.
----------------------------------------

Information to hand shows that the Shanghai
Branch of the Social Movement Direction Committee,
527 Range Road, is sponsoring the holding of a
celebration on July 28 in respect of the recognition
of the Nanking Government by Germany, Italy and
other pro-Axis Powers.

Shops, industrial organizations etc. in
the Western District, O.O.L., have received a circular
notice (translation attached and marked "A") to the
effect that at least two persons be detailed by each
shop to take part in a lantern procession to be held
at 6.30 p.m. July 28. The men will assemble in the
vicinity of the Jessfield Park and then proceed along
Brenan Road, Jessfield Road, Yu Yuen Road, Edinburgh
Road and Great Western Road in the extra-Settlement
Roads area.

It is learned that posters will also be
posted on buses, trams and taxis of the four leading
garages by the labour unions of these public utility
workers.

Three "Pai-Lous" are being erected, one on
Bubbling Well Road to the west of Foo Ping Road,
another at Old West Gate, Nantao, and the third at the
former premises of the Chinese Chamber of Commerce on
North Soochow Road.

However, final decision by the Nanking
authorities is being awaited as to whether or not the
celebration will be held as scheduled.

According to information from the Shanghai
Special Municipal Government, it was originally
page_data.zh:
S.1, 特务科。
1941年7月23日。

为庆祝德国及其他轴心国承认国民政府（南京），将于7月28日在西区举行灯笼游行。
---

现有情报显示，位于兰心路527号的社会运动指导委员会上海分会正在赞助于7月28日举行庆祝活动，以纪念德国、意大利及其他亲轴心国国家承认南京政府。

西区的商店、工业组织等（O.O.L.）已收到通函（附译文并标记为“A”），内容是要求每家商店至少派出两人参加将于7月28日下午6:30举行的灯笼游行。人员将在极司菲尔公园附近集合，然后沿布伦南路、极司菲尔路、愚园路、爱丁堡路和大西路在越界筑路区域行进。

据悉，这些公用事业工人的工会还将在四家主要车行的巴士、电车和出租车上张贴海报。

三座“牌楼”正在搭建中，一座位于福平路以西的静安寺路上，另一座位于南市老西门，第三座位于苏州河北路原中国商会会所旧址。

然而，南京当局仍在等待最终决定，以确定庆祝活动是否按计划举行。

据上海特别市政府的情报，最初

page_data.en:
- 2 -

decided that the celebration of the recognition by
the Axis Powers of the Nanking Government was to
have been sponsored by the Special Municipal
Government on July 18, but it was subsequently
cancelled in deference to instructions from Nanking
to the effect that all official bodies under the
control of the government must not hold celebrations,
but any voluntary gestures on the part of public
organizations are not to be interfered with. On
this account, the Shanghai Special Municipal Government
has appropriated a sum of $3,000 to the Shanghai
Branch of the Social Movement Direction Committee
to be spent for this purpose.

Information from Shanghai Municipality
Wharf Coolies' Unions, Pootung, reveals that the
press reports on the celebration are purely propaganda
and that instructions from superior organizations
have not yet been received as to the programme of the
celebrations and whether or not the celebrations will
be actually held on July 28.

According to latest information received,
the Shanghai Branch of the Social Movement Direction
Committee, 527 Range Road, will hold a celebration
meeting of local people at the Chinese Chamber of
Commerce, North Soochow Road, at 10 a.m. July 28.
Instructions to this effect, together with rules
and slogans, (translations attached and marked
"B", "C" and "D") have been issued by the Committee.

Certified true copy

〔此处转录不清〕
CSC.
page_data.zh:
- 2 -

决定由上海特别市政府于7月18日主办庆祝轴心国承认南京政府的活动，但随后鉴于南京方面的指示，即政府控制下的所有官方机构不得举行庆祝活动，而公共团体的自愿举动不予干涉，该活动遂被取消。为此，上海特别市政府已拨出3,000元给社会运动指导委员会上海分会，用于此项目的开支。

来自上海市浦东码头工人工会的消息显示，关于庆祝活动的新闻报道纯属宣传，且尚未收到上级组织关于庆祝活动方案以及是否确实于7月28日举行庆祝活动的指示。

根据收到的最新消息，位于兰路527号的社会运动指导委员会上海分会，将于7月28日上午10时在苏州河北路的中国总商会举行当地民众庆祝大会。委员会已发布相关指示，连同规则和标语（译文附后，标记为“B”、“C”和“D”）。

核证无误副本

CSC.

Translation of a notice issued by the "Meeting of the
People of the Shanghai Special Municipality, to Celebrate
the Recognition of the National Government (Nanking) by
Germany, Italy and six other countries" containing a set

people of Shanghai.
------------------------------------------------------------------------

MEASURES GOVERNING THE CELEBRATION OF THE
RECOGNITION OF THE NATIONAL GOVERNMENT
(NANKING) BY GERMANY, ITALY AND SIX OTHER
COUNTRIES.

(1) Shops, dwelling houses, factories, public bodies
and official organizations throughout this
Municipality should hoist flags and put up
decorations.
(2) Fire crackers will be set off at noon.
(3) Each family should prepare at least two lanterns
for the purpose of taking part in the lantern
procession.
(4) Shops and factories should appoint two delegates
each to participate in the lantern procession.
(5) Date and venue of the procession will form the
subject of a further notice.

Meeting of the People of the Shanghai

“上海特别市市民庆祝德、意等六国承认国民政府（南京）大会”发布的通告译文，其中包含上海市民庆祝此次活动的一套措施。
---

关于庆祝德、意等六国承认国民政府（南京）的措施。

(1) 本市各商店、住宅、工厂、公共团体及官方组织应悬挂旗帜并布置装饰。
(2) 中午燃放鞭炮。
(3) 每户家庭应至少准备两盏灯笼，以便参加提灯游行。
(4) 各商店和工厂应各指派两名代表参加提灯游行。
(5) 游行的日期和地点将另行通知。
（通告上盖有印章：7月28日下午6时30分）

上海特别市市民庆祝德、意等六国承认国民政府（南京）大会。

（还盖有上海西区公民联合会曹家渡分会的印章）

核证无误副本。

W.H. Richardson
CSC.

page_data.en:
B
Translation of Order No.463 (Character 〔此处转录不清〕 ),
dated July 15, 1941, issued by the Shanghai Branch
of the Social Movement Direction Committee.
------------------------------------------------------------

In view of the fact that the recognition of the
National Government (Nanking Government) successively
by Germany, Italy, Rumania, Slovakia, Croatia, Spain,
Hungary and Bulgaria sufficiently reveals that the
movement of national reconstruction by means of peace
and anti-Comintern has attained international understanding
and sympathy, thereby strengthening the position of our
Government in the world, people in the various walks of
life in Shanghai have held meetings and prepared to hold
a general celebration meeting on July 28 in order to
express their enthusiastic support of the National
Government. All public bodies should hoist the
national flag and post handbills outside their own
offices on that day in celebration of the occasion.
Attached to this order is a copy of the scheme and
slogans for the celebrations.

(Chopped) Shanghai Branch, Social Move-
ment Direction Committee.
(Signed) Sung Ming Chi (孫鳴岐),
Chairman.
( " ) Chiang Yung Pao (蔣文宝),
Vice-Chairman.

Certified true copy

Richardson
CSC.
page_data.zh:
B
1941年7月15日由社会运动指导委员会上海分会发布的第463号命令（字号〔此处转录不清〕）译文。
---

鉴于德国、意大利、罗马尼亚、斯洛伐克、克罗地亚、西班牙、匈牙利和保加利亚相继承认国民政府（南京政府），充分表明通过和平与反共手段进行国家重建的运动已获得国际理解与同情，从而加强了我国政府在世界上的地位，上海各界人士已举行会议，并准备于7月28日举行盛大庆祝大会，以表达对国民政府的热情支持。所有公共团体应在当天悬挂国旗并在其办公处外张贴传单，以资庆祝。随令附上庆祝活动的方案及标语副本。

（盖章）社会运动指导委员会上海分会。
（签名）孙鸣岐 (Sung Ming Chi)，主席。
（同上）蒋文宝 (Chiang Yung Pao)，副主席。

核证无误副本

Richardson
CSC.

page_data.en:
C

Preparations for participation by local
citizens in a lantern procession in
celebration of the recognition of the
National Government (Nanking) by Germany,
Italy and six other nations.
------------------------------------------

Preparation of lantern

Every organization taking part in the procession
should prepare at least two large, smart and handsome
lanterns with the following inscriptions: "Celebration
by the people of the Shanghai Special Municipality of
the recognition of the National Government by Germany,
Italy and six other nations." In addition, a number of
small lanterns with inscriptions: "Celebration of the
recognition of the National Government by Germany and
other nations" are to be prepared to be on display
during the procession.

Number of Participants

Each organization should be represented by at
least ten persons in the procession.

Venue

Jessfield Park.

Date of lantern procession

A further notice will be issued.

Awards

All the expenses for the making of lanterns,
etc. are to be borne by the organizations taking part
in the procession. However, awards will be given to
those organizations which are more numerically
represented and which display handsome lanterns in
the procession.

Certified true copy

〔此处为手写签名，难以辨认〕
CSC.
page_data.zh:
C

当地市民参加提灯游行以庆祝德、意等六国承认国民政府（南京）的准备工作。
---

灯笼准备

每个参加游行的组织应至少准备两盏大型、精美且美观的灯笼，上书：“上海特别市市民庆祝德、意等六国承认国民政府”。此外，还需准备若干写有“庆祝德等国承认国民政府”的小灯笼，以便在游行期间展示。

参与人数

每个组织在游行中至少应有十人代表参加。

地点

兆丰公园 (Jessfield Park)。

提灯游行日期

另行通知。

奖励

制作灯笼等所有费用由参加游行的组织自行承担。然而，将对那些参与人数较多且在游行中展示精美灯笼的组织给予奖励。

核证无误副本

〔此处为手写签名，难以辨认〕
CSC.

page_data.en:
D

Slogans

1. Celebrate the recognition of the National Government
by Germany, Italy and other friendly nations.
2. Strengthen the National Government and accelerate the
achievement of complete peace.
3. Strengthen the East Asia Axis and establish a new
order in East Asia.
4. Let the Asia Axis nations unite and establish a
new world order.
5. Destroy the old order of International Jingoism.
6. Construct a new order for the mutual prosperity
of the nations.
7. Down with Communism.
8. Exterminate Chungking Regime, the supporter of the
old order.
9. Long live the Axis nations.
10. Long live the Emancipation of the Chinese race.

Certified true copy.

〔此处为手写签名〕
CSC.
page_data.zh:
D

标语

1. 庆祝德、意及其他友好国家承认国民政府。
2. 加强国民政府，加速实现全面和平。
3. 加强东亚轴心，建立东亚新秩序。
4. 让轴心国团结起来，建立世界新秩序。
5. 摧毁国际沙文主义的旧秩序。
6. 构建各国共同繁荣的新秩序。
7. 打倒共产主义。
8. 消灭旧秩序的支持者重庆政权。
9. 轴心国万岁。
10. 中华民族解放万岁。

核证无误副本。

〔此处为手写签名〕
CSC.

Translation of Order No.463 (Character Woo "沪"),
dated July 15, 1941, issued by the Shanghai Branch
of the Social Movement Direction Committee

In view of the fact that the recognition of the
National Government (Nanking Government) successively
by Germany, Italy, Rumania, Slovakia, Croatia, Spain,
Hungary and Bulgaria sufficiently reveals that the
movement of national reconstruction by means of peace
and anti-Comintern has attained international understanding
and sympathy, thereby strengthening the position of our
government in the world, people in the various walks of
life in Shanghai have held meetings and prepared to hold
a general celebration meeting on July 28 in order to
express their enthusiastic support of the National
Government. All public bodies should hoist the
national flag and post handbills outside their own
offices on that day in celebration of the occasion.
Attached to this order is a copy of the scheme and
slogans for the celebrations.

(Chopped) Shanghai Branch, Social Movement
Direction Committee.

Chairman.

Preparations for participation by local
citizens in a lantern procession in
celebration of the recognition of the
National Government (Nanking) by Germany,
Italy and six other nations.

Preparation of lanterns

Every organization taking part in the procession
should prepare at least two large, smart and handsome
lanterns with the following inscriptions: "Celebration
by the people of the Shanghai Special Municipality of
the recognition of the National Government by Germany,
Italy and six other nations." In addition, a number of
small lanterns with inscriptions: "Celebration of the
Recognition of the National Government by Germany and
other nations" are to be prepared to be on display
during the procession.

Number of Participants

Each organization should be represented by at
least ten persons in the procession.

Venue

Jessfield Park.

Date of lantern procession

A further notice will be issued.

Awards

All the expenses for the making of lanterns,
etc. are to be borne by the organizations taking part
in the procession. However, awards will be given to
those organizations which are more numerically
represented and which display handsome lanterns in
the procession.

当地市民参加庆祝德、意等六国承认国民政府（南京）灯笼游行的准备工作。

灯笼制作

凡参加游行的各组织应至少准备两盏大型、精美且美观的灯笼，上书：“上海特别市市民庆祝德、意等六国承认国民政府”。此外，还需准备若干小型灯笼，上书：“庆祝德意等国承认国民政府”，以便在游行期间展示。

参与人数

各组织在游行中应至少有十名代表参加。

地点

极司菲尔公园（Jessfield Park）。

灯笼游行日期

将另行通知。

奖励

制作灯笼等所有费用由参加游行的各组织自行承担。然而，对于在游行中派出人数较多且展示精美灯笼的组织，将给予奖励。

SHANGHAI DAILY NEWS.

Procession Planned to
Celebrate Recognition

A lantern procession will be held
either tonight or tomorrow night in
Shanghai to celebrate the recognition
of the new Nanking régime by eight
Axis powers. It is reported in the
"Chinese American Daily News"
that local supporters of the new
régime have been forcing people to
participate in the procession, to hang
out flags and to let off fire-crackers.
It is said that in addition to forcing
people in occupied districts to cele-
brate the occasion, the new régime
has sponsored a similar movement
in Shanghai. "Meaningless" activities
may be started in foreign areas here
and because of this, the police began
taking strict precautions on Tues-
day.
The report indicates that the lan-
tern procession may be held in the
outside road areas and that Jessfield
Park may be used as the starting
point of the procession.
Meanwhile, a report from Chung-
king yesterday stated that the Brit-
ish Ambassador to China officially
notified the Ministry of Foreign
Affairs at Chungking on July 16 of
London's recognition of the National
Government at Chungking as the
Chinese government.
A statement made by Mr. Anthony
Eden, the British Foreign Secretary,
in answer to a question in the House
of Commons on July 9 reaffirming
the British policy in this respect
was said to have been mentioned in
the Ambassador's note to which the
Chinese Foreign Minister made a
reply.

1941年7月26日

《上海日报》。

计划举行游行以庆祝承认

今晚或明晚将在上海举行灯笼游行，以庆祝八个轴心国承认新的南京政权。据《中美日报》报道，新政权的地方支持者一直强迫民众参加游行、悬挂旗帜并燃放鞭炮。据说，除了强迫占领区民众庆祝这一事件外，新政权还在上海发起了类似的运动。在此间的外国区域可能会开始一些“毫无意义”的活动，因此，警方于周二开始采取严格预防措施。
报道指出，灯笼游行可能在越界筑路区域举行，极司菲尔公园可能被用作游行的起点。
与此同时，来自重庆的一份报告昨日称，英国驻华大使于7月16日正式通知重庆外交部，伦敦承认重庆国民政府为中国政府。
据悉，英国外交大臣安东尼·艾登先生于7月9日在下议院回答提问时发表的一项声明，重申了英国在此方面的政策，该声明被提及在大使致中国外交部长的照会中，中国外交部长对此作了回复。

November 30, 1940

New Central Government - local celebration.

In celebration of the proposed recognition
of the Nanking Government by Japan and the assumption
of office by Mr. Wang Ching Wei as Chairman of the
New Government, posters were issued to members of the
Western District organizations for distribution this
morning, November 30. The propaganda purports to
have emanated from the Shanghai Branch of the Social
Movement Direction Committee, and the Shanghai Special
Municipality Kuomintang Headquarters. The posters
contain the following slogans :

(1) Support Chairman Wang Ching Wei.
(2) Long Live Chairman Wang Ching Wei
(3) Down with the Traitorous Communist Party.
(4) Support the Sino-Japanese Agreement for
protection against Communism.
(5) The conclusion of the Sino-Japanese Pact will
bring about peace.
(6) The conclusion of the Sino-Japanese Pact is
the successful fruits of the Peace Movement
and the beginning of an era of Peace.
(7) Let all local residents celebrate the con-
clusion of the Sino-Japanese Pact.
(8) Support Wang Ching Wei in enforcing the
principles of the late National Father.
(9) Let China and Japan cooperate forever and
oppose the third party nations who are
instigating dissension.

November 28, 1940.

Information from a confidential and reliable
source to the effect that the Nanking Government is
expecting recognition from Tokyo in the very near
future and has set aside the sum of $50,000 to cover
expenses for a celebration of the event. The
celebrations are expected to be carried out at the
beginning of December, and it is reported from the
same source that in Shanghai a lantern procession will
be staged which will be composed of the labour elements
connected with the unions in Nantao and the Western
District. This procession is expected to pass
through the Settlement and French Concession but
details are at present lacking. Preparations are
in progress among the labour organizations affiliated
with the Wang Ching Wei regime and every endeavour
will be made to get details beforehand.

SECRET
Military Affairs Commission of Nanking
Government - orders cessation of recruiting
guerillas.

November 11, 1940.

In compliance with the instructions of Mr. Wang
Ching Wei, Acting Chairman of the National Government
(Nanking) and Chairman of the Military Affairs Commission,
the "Recruiting and Reorganizing Committee(点編委員會)"
of the Military Affairs Commission was dissolved at the
beginning of November. Instructions were also issued
by the Commission to the different pacification headquarters
that they should cease recruiting forthwith. Meanwhile
circular notices were issued to the military and civil
organs of the various cities informing them of the above
instructions, and on November 7, notices were published in
the Ping Pao and Central China Daily News announcing the
dissolution of the committee in question, and ordering
the cessation of recruiting of irregular units adding that
any one found engaging in such activity would be severely
punished.

It is to be noted that the "Recruiting and
Reorganizing Committee" of the Military Affairs Commission
was formed subsequent to the inauguration of the Nanking
Government in March, 1940. The following are the present
members of the Standing Committee:-

Chow Fuh Hai(周佛海), Minister of Police and
Minister of Finance.
Bao Wen Yueh(鮑文), Minister of War.
Yang Kwei(楊揆一), Chief staff officer of the
Military Affairs Commission.

The principal mission of this Committee was to
recruit and reorganize the guerilla units scattered
throughout Kiangsu and Chekiang provinces but those
guerillas must each be in possession of arms if were to
be incorporated.

南京军事委员会
政府——下令停止招募游击队。

1940年11月11日。

遵照国民政府（南京）代理主席兼军事委员会委员长汪精卫先生的指示，军事委员会“点编委员会”于11月初解散。委员会亦向各绥靖总部发出指令，要求立即停止招募。同时，向各城市的军政机关发出通函，告知上述指令；并于11月7日在《平报》和《华中日报》刊登公告，宣布解散该委员会，并命令停止招募非正规部队，补充说明任何被发现从事此类活动的人将受到严厉惩罚。

值得注意的是，军事委员会的“点编委员会”是在1940年3月南京政府成立之后组建的。目前常务委员会成员如下：-

周佛海，警政部长兼财政部长。
鲍文岳(音译)，军政部长。
杨揆一，军事委员会参谋长。

该委员会的主要任务是招募和重组散布在江苏和浙江省的游击队单位，但这些游击队必须各自拥有武器才能被收编。

（左侧批注/印章区域）：
机密
S & C G

It has frequently happened that those guerillas
thus reorganized have turned against the Nanking
Government when coming in contact with troops belonging
to the Chungking Government. It is learned that
at the beginning of October this year, some 4,000
members of the reorganized units under the command of
Ning Yuen Dao (任援道), Pacification Commander of
the Nanking Government, were despatched to the border
of Kiangsu and Anhwei provinces to engage the New 4th
Army, but shortly after arrival, more than half of
their numbers deserted to the New 4th Army and similar
incidents have often happened at other places.

Because of those circumstances, Mr. Wang Ching Wei
knowing the unreliable nature of the reorganized mobile
units, issued the above instructions.

The following is the established strength of the
military units between Shanghai and Hangchow and Nanking:-

经常发生的情况是，这些被重组的游击队在与重庆政府的部队接触时，转而反对南京政府。据悉，今年10月初，南京政府绥靖司令任援道指挥下的约4,000名重组部队成员被派往江苏和安徽边境与新四军作战，但抵达后不久，其中一半以上的人员投奔了新四军，类似事件在其他地方也屡有发生。

鉴于这些情况，汪精卫先生深知重组后的流动部队不可靠，遂发出了上述指令。

Peiping Changing Flags Again
Sun-In-Blue-Sky
Makes Comeback

Police Ordering Shops
To Prepare Emblems
For April 1

(Reuter's Agency)
PEIPING, Mar. 28.—The local police are reported to have notified various shops and stores in Peiping to have a "Sun in Blue Sky" flag made for use on April 1 on the occasion of the inauguration of the new central government at Nanking.
The new flag is similar to that used in Chungking, except for a small pennant at the top bearing four Chinese characters in red signifying anti-communism and peace.
All preparations have been completed in Peiping and Tientsin to celebrate the inauguration.
In Peiping, according to Chinese reports posters will be placarded throughout the city, floral "Pai Lous" will be erected at different thoroughfares, and here will be a mass celebration.
In Tientsin, the same reports state, there will be a three day program of festivities, which will include lantern and flag processions, mass celebrations in the auditorium of the Tientsin Municipality, placarding of posters all over the city, and the holding of a reception for foreign Consuls.

Wang Keh-min Returns
(Havas)
PEKING, Mar. 25.—Mr. Wang Keh-min, Chairman of the Peking Provisional Government, returned here by plane this afternoon from Nanking, where he attended the meeting of the Central Political Council.
He was accompanied by Mr. Chu Chen Minister of Justice in the Provisional Government, and General Chi Hsueh-yuan, Minister for Public Order.
The abolition of the Provisional Government has been fixed for March 29 and the inauguration of the North China Political Affairs Council for the following day. The personnel of the Council will remain that of the Provisional Government.
page_data.zh:
北平再次换旗
青天白日旗
卷土重来

警方命令商店
准备徽章
供4月1日使用

(路透社)
北平，3月28日。—据报道，当地警方已通知北平各家商铺，为4月1日南京新中央政府成立典礼制作“青天白日”旗以备使用。
新旗帜与重庆使用的旗帜相似，不同之处在于顶部有一面小三角旗，上面用红色写着四个汉字，象征反共与和平。
北平和天津为庆祝成立典礼所做的准备工作均已就绪。
据中文报道，在北平，海报将张贴在全市各处，主要街道将搭建花卉装饰的“牌楼”，并将举行群众庆祝活动。
据同一报道，在天津，将举行为期三天的庆祝活动，包括灯笼和旗帜游行、在天津市公会堂举行群众庆祝大会、在全市张贴海报，以及举行招待外国领事的酒会。

王克敏返回
(哈瓦斯通讯社)
北平，3月25日。—北平临时政府主席王克敏先生今天下午乘飞机从南京返回此地，他此前参加了中央政治委员会会议。
陪同他回来的有临时政府司法部长朱深先生和治安总长齐燮元将军。
临时政府的废除定于3月29日，华北政务委员会将于次日成立。委员会的人员构成将保持与临时政府相同。

REPORT
Date January 29 1940.

Subject Conference in Tsingtao reported not very successful.

Made by. and Forwarded by Supt. Tan Shao Liang

Information has been received from a reliable source (Pro-Japanese) that Wang Ching Wei has not been very successful in the conference that took place at Tsingtao where the heads of the Provisional and Reformed Governments discussed with him measures to form the Political Council without which it will be impossible to organize a new Central Government.

The principal cause for disagreement between Wang Ching Wei and his rivals who are backed up by different Japanese military leaders, would appear to be the right of choosing and appointing pro-Japanese elements for the position as members of the Political Council. It will be these members who will organize the new government and it is therefore important when viewed in the light of whether Wang Ching Wei or his rivals will possess the superior number of men serving on the Political Council. Besides the Japanese demand a say as to those appointed and it remains to be seen whether Wang is going to give in and continue his services in the administration without freedom like the other puppets. As pointed out in previous reports, the Japanese military in China have already given up hope of making peace with Chungking but at the same time if Wang Ching Wei should be successful in his peace talks with Chungking officials, his position would undoubtedly be strengthened but should he not succeed with them his Government when formed would be in danger of collapsing after inauguration.

由谭绍良督察长制作并转呈

从可靠来源（亲日派）获悉，汪精卫在青岛举行的会议上并未取得很大成功，会上临时政府和维新政府的首脑与他讨论了组建政治委员会的措施，若无此委员会，就不可能组织新的中央政府。

汪精卫与其竞争对手（得到不同日本军事领导人的支持）之间分歧的主要原因，似乎是选择和支持亲日分子担任政治委员会成员的权利。正是这些成员将组建新政府，因此，从汪精卫或其竞争对手谁将在政治委员会中占据多数席位的角度来看，这一点至关重要。此外，日本人对任命人选要求有发言权，汪精卫是否会让步并在没有自由的情况下像其他傀儡一样继续服务于行政机构，尚待观察。正如之前报告所指出的，在华日军已经放弃了与重庆达成和平的希望，但同时，如果汪精卫成功与重庆官员进行和平谈判，他的地位无疑会得到加强；但如果他未能成功，他的政府在成立后将面临垮台的危险。

January 24, 1940. Afternoon Translation.

Chinese-American Daily News, Ta Mei Pao, Sin Wan Pao, Shun
Pao, National Herald, Hwa Pao (Chungking telegram) :-

GENERAL CHIANG KAI-SHEK ISSUES OPEN LETTER TO PEOPLE ON
SECRET PACT CONCLUDED BETWEEN WANG CHING-WEI AND JAPAN

General Chiang Kai-shek has issued the
following open letter addressed to the people throughout
the country on the secret pact concluded between Wang Ching-
wei and Japan:-

Recently, Chinese and foreign newspapers
published a humiliating document known as the "Principles
for the readjustment of new relations between Japan and
China" which Wang Ching-wei and the Japanese had concluded
in Shanghai and was taken to Tokyo by Inoukai with
the conditions submitted by Wang Ching-wei to the Japanese
for the creation of a puppet regime, and the reply from the
Japanese.

I am sure that the people throughout the
country, after reading these documents, will have gained a
deeper insight into the treacherous schemes of the Japanese
and Wang Ching-wei. Through the revelations made by these
documents we can now understand the underhand activities
between the Japanese and the puppet authorities during the
past few months and the results of the discussions held by
the Japanese Asia Development Board a month ago. Before these
documents were published, we were already convinced that
Wang Ching-wei would unhesitatingly barter away the whole
nation and the life of China's future generations.

FILE
I want the people to study these documents
carefully and then to read my speech of December, 1938,
denouncing Prince Konoye's statement. A comparison between
the "Principles for the readjustment of new relations between
Japan and China" and Prince Konoye's statement will prove
that my criticisms made a year ago are correct. I declared
at that time that Japan's real desire was to annex the whole
of China and to annihilate the Chinese people and that Prince
Konoye's statement was an admission of Japan's ambition to
dominate East Asia and then to conquer the world. To-day
my words have been proved to be correct. The "Principles for
the readjustment of new relations between Japan and China"
gives definite shape to Prince Konoya's statement.

(批：Chinese attacked for...)
This pact between Japan and the puppet
authorities is ten times more severe than the 21 Demands
and even harsher than the measures adopted by Japan to
enslave Korea. I firmly believe that all righteous-minded
Chinese people cannot help being infuriated upon reading
such a document.

During the past year Wang Ching-wei has been
shamelessly propagating a peace which, he states, will not
harm China's independence or liberty; he has also been
clamouring for "good relations with neighbouring countries,"
a "common front against communism" and "an economic rapprochement."
From the pact concluded between Wang Ching-wei and the
Japanese, we can understand the significance of these three
expressions which, for the benefit of the people, I shall
put briefly as follows:-

The so-called "good relations with neighbouring
countries" means the incorporation of China with Japan."
The "common front against communism" is tantamount to the
maintaining of a perpetual garrison in China by Japan. The

《中美日报》、《大美晚报》、《新闻报》、《申报》、《国民公报》、《华报》（重庆电）：-

蒋介石将军就汪精卫与日本缔结之秘密协定向全国民众发表公开信

蒋介石将军就汪精卫与日本缔结之秘密协定，向全国民众发表如下公开信：-

近日，中外报刊刊登了一份名为《调整中日新关系原则》的屈辱性文件，该文件系汪精卫与日本方面在上海达成，并由犬养健（Inoukai）带往东京，内容包括汪精卫向日本提出的建立傀儡政权的条件以及日本的答复。

我相信，全国民众在阅读这些文件后，将对日本和汪精卫的奸险阴谋有更深刻的认识。通过这些文件所揭露的内容，我们现在可以了解过去几个月间日本与傀儡当局之间的幕后活动，以及一个月前日本东亚发展委员会（注：原文为 Asia Development Board，通常指兴亚院或类似机构，此处依原文直译或理解为相关决策机构）讨论的结果。在这些文件公布之前，我们就已确信，汪精卫会毫不犹豫地出卖整个国家及中国子孙后代的生存权利。

档案

我希望民众仔细研究这些文件，然后阅读我于1938年12月发表的谴责近卫亲王声明的演讲。将《调整中日新关系原则》与近卫亲王的声明进行比较，将证明我一年前的批评是正确的。我当时宣称，日本的真实欲望是吞并整个中国并消灭中国人民，而近卫亲王的声明承认了日本主宰东亚进而征服世界的野心。今天，我的话已被证明是正确的。《调整中日新关系原则》使近卫亲王的声明具体化。

（批注：中国人受到攻击因为...）

日本与傀儡当局之间的这项协定比“二十一条”苛刻十倍，甚至比日本奴役朝鲜所采取的措施更为严酷。我坚信，所有有良知的中国人在阅读此类文件时，无不感到愤怒。

在过去的一年里，汪精卫一直无耻地宣扬一种他声称不会损害中国独立或自由的“和平”；他还鼓吹“善邻友好”、“共同防共”和“经济提携”。从汪精卫与日本缔结的协定中，我们可以理解这三个表述的含义，为了民众的利益，我简要概括如下：-

所谓“善邻友好”意味着将中国与日本合并。“共同防共”等同于日本在中国永久驻军。而

page_data.en:
January 24, 1940. Afternoon Translation.

expression "economic rapprochement" is nothing less than
the economic domination of China by Japan. This is what
Japan expects after Wang Ching-wei has enslaved China.
I have no desire to elucidate one by one all
the harsh terms contained in the pact; I will, however,
deal with some of the more important points. Firstly, let
us examine some of the main points:-
(1) Under the theory of "constructing a New
Order in East Asia" and "good relations with neighbouring
countries," it is intended to bring about rapprochement
among Japan, China and Manchukuo. The day that such a
rapprochement is effected will see an end to the indepen-
dence of our country.
(2) It is proposed to demark North China and
Mongolia as a region for a strong union of national defence
and economic affairs and the creation of a special military
and political status in Mongolia. Now, let me ask, whose
national defence is meant by this so-called national defence?
Can China be called an independent country when she has to
create a special status in her own territory for the
co-operation with Japan in the matter of national defence?
(3) The creation of a region in the Lower Yangtze
for close economic co-operation simply means that what China
possesses belongs to Japan and what China owns Japan has the
right to take.
(4) The creation of special positions on islands
along the South China coast will mean the cessation of free
trade between China and foreign countries and turn that
region into a Japanese base in the event of a war between
Japan and any European Power on the Pacific or Indian Oceans.
Secondly, the section dealing with "good
relations with neighbouring countries" contain the following
points:-
(1) Infinite rapprochement.
(2) The adoption of chain-like measures for the
whole scheme. The "chain" is tantamount to the fettering of
future generations.
The term "infinite rapprochement" is one newly
invented by Japan. Wang Ching-wei has said that he under-
stands the general outline of Prince Konoye's statement, but
does he realize that Japan is demanding "infinite rapprochement"
Wang Ching-wei's newspaper organs have shamelessly announced
that economic co-operation would be limited, but the Japanese
want "infinite rapprochement." What does the word "infinite"
mean? We have a term in Chinese meaning "boundless completeness".
Therefore the word "infinite" means "boundless" or "endless".
Apart from affiliation, there can be no rapprochement between
two sides of such a boundless or endless character. Such a
rapprochement would be nothing less than subjugation.
(3) Before Japan and Manchukuo can respect the
sovereign and territorial rights of China, the puppet regime
must first recognize Manchukuo. Can recognition of Manchukuo
State be regarded as showing respect towards the sovereign
and territorial rights of China? China does not need respect
for her sovereign and territorial rights from the puppet state
of Manchukuo, which in reality forms part of China's territory.
Is such respect mentioned by the Japanese a kind of jest or
is it to be of the nature of an insult?

“经济提携”一词无非是日本对中国的经济支配。这就是日本在汪精卫奴役中国之后所期望得到的。

我不愿逐一阐释协定中包含的所有苛刻条款；然而，我将处理其中一些更重要的要点。首先，让我们审视一些主要点：-
(1) 在“建设东亚新秩序”和“善邻友好”的理论下，旨在促成日本、中国和满洲国之间的亲善。这种亲善实现之日，即是我国独立终结之时。
(2) 提议将华北和蒙古划定为国防和经济事务强力联合的区域，并在蒙古建立特殊的军事和政治地位。现在，我要问，这种所谓的国防是指谁的国防？当一个国家必须在其领土内为与日本在国防事务上的合作而设立特殊地位时，还能称其为独立国家吗？
(3) 在长江下游地区建立一个紧密经济合作区，仅仅意味着中国所拥有的归日本所有，中国所有的日本有权拿走。
(4) 在华南沿海岛屿设立特殊地位，将意味着中国与外国之间自由贸易的终止，并在日本与任何欧洲强国在太平洋或印度洋发生战争时，将该地区变成日本的基地。
其次，关于“善邻友好”的部分包含以下几点：-
(1) 无限亲善。
(2) 对整个方案采取连锁措施。“连锁”等同于束缚子孙后代。
“无限亲善”是日本新发明的术语。汪精卫曾说，他理解近卫亲王声明的大致轮廓，但他是否意识到日本要求的是“无限亲善”？汪精卫的新闻机构无耻地宣布经济合作将是有限的，但日本想要的是“无限亲善”。“无限”一词是什么意思？我们中文里有一个词意思是“无边的完整”。因此，“无限”一词意味着“无边”或“无尽”。除了隶属关系外，双方之间不可能存在这种无边或无尽性质的亲善。这种亲善无非就是征服。
(3) 在日本和满洲国尊重中国的主权和领土权利之前，傀儡政权必须首先承认满洲国。承认满洲国能被视为对中国主权和领土权利的尊重吗？中国不需要实际上构成中国领土一部分的满洲国傀儡国家对其主权和领土权利的尊重。日本人提到的这种尊重是一种玩笑，还是一种侮辱？

page_data.en:
January 24, 1940. Afternoon Translation

(4) The suppression of propaganda and
education as well as of political administration, commercial
affairs and foreign policy that are detrimental to mutual
co-operation and friendship between the two countries mean;
in other words, that all matters or events in China that
are regarded as unfavourable to Japan should be suppressed
(5) In her relations with third Powers, China
should adopt a policy that does not violate the fundamental
principles for mutual rapprochement and co-operation between
China and Japan. This is tantamount to asking China to
listen to Japan in all matters relating to China's diplomacy
in other words, it deprives China of her freedom and
independence. Does not this mean that China is to be
converted into a Japanese protectorate? Moreover, Japanese
advisors are to be employed by the new Central Government
who will be detailed to those places where strong
co-operation is necessary and to specially designated
areas. This means that Japan desires to place China
under her supervision through the medium of these advisors.
(6) Co-operation in cultural assimilation and
inventions means that China will hereafter be deprived of
her independent culture and be denied the right to make
new cultural inventions.
(7) In the measures governing the so-called
"joint defence," co-operation not only in the joint
suppression of communism but also in the joint maintenance
of peace and order is stipulated. This term "the joint
maintenance of peace and order" can only mean the conversion
of the whole of China into garrison areas for Japanese
troops, and that Japan will have the right to station
troops in any part of this country.
(8) The stationing of Japanese troops in North
China and at various strategic points in Mongolia for anti-
communist purposes; the conclusion of a military alliance
against communism; the recognition by China of Japan's
right to station warships at various specially designated
parts along the Yangtse and on various islands in South
China by the Japanese fleet --- all these places are far
away from Soviet Russia, Japan's imaginary foe, therefore
the term "anti-communism" is not applicable. For this
reason, the term "joint maintenance of peace and order"
is employed to fit the case.
According to these measures, Japan reserves
the right to secure for military purposes control of *
railways, aviation, communications along leading waterways
and harbours in the areas wherein Japanese troops are
stationed, while China's military and police and defence
preparations by China are to be reduced to the minimum and
must be carried out with the co-operation of the Japanese
advisors. What does this "co-operation" mean? It is
nothing but supervision and control.
(9) Now let us examine the meaning of the so-
called economic rapprochement. It first demands mutual
guarantees and then an economic alliance. It aims at the
seizure of all the economic resources of China and the
control of her financial and economic policy as well as
her Customs tariff.

1940年1月24日。下午译件

(4) 压制宣传和教育，以及压制对两国相互合作与友谊有害的政治行政、商业事务和外交政策，换句话说，意味着应压制中国境内所有被视为对日本不利的事项或事件。
(5) 在与第三国的关系中，中国应采取不违反中日相互亲善与合作基本原则的政策。这等同于要求中国在与外交有关的一切事务上听从日本，换句话说，它剥夺了中国的自由和独立。这难道不意味着中国将被转变为日本的保护国吗？此外，新的中央政府将聘请日本顾问，他们将被派往需要强力合作的地点和特别指定的区域。这意味着日本希望通过这些顾问将中国置于其监督之下。
(6) 文化同化和发明方面的合作，意味着中国此后将被剥夺其独立文化，并被否认进行新文化发明的权利。
(7) 在所谓“共同防卫”的措施中，规定不仅在联合镇压共产主义方面进行合作，而且在联合维持治安方面也要合作。“联合维持治安”这一术语只能意味着将整个中国变为日军的驻防区，日本有权在该国的任何地方驻扎军队。
(8) 以反共为目的在华北和蒙古各战略要点驻扎日军；缔结反共军事同盟；中国承认日本舰队在中国长江沿线各特别指定部分和华南各岛屿驻扎军舰的权利——所有这些地点都远离日本假想的敌人苏联俄罗斯，因此“反共”一词并不适用。出于这个原因，使用了“联合维持治安”一词以符合情况。
根据这些措施，日本保留为军事目的控制日军驻扎区域内的铁路、航空、主要水道沿线的通讯和港口的权利，而中国的军事、警察和防御准备将减少到最低限度，并且必须在日本顾问的合作下进行。这种“合作”是什么意思？它无非就是监督和控制。
(9) 现在让我们审视所谓经济提携的含义。它首先要求相互保证，然后是经济联盟。其目标是夺取中国所有的经济资源，并控制其财政和经济政策以及关税税率。

page_data.en:
January 24, 1940. Afternoon Translation

(10) As regards the matters relating to the development of China's resources, the Customs tariff, aviation, communications and meteorology, a pact is to be reached which will be entirely in accordance with the requirements of Japan.
(11) As for the development and utilization of resources, Japan will enjoy special facilities in North China and Inner Mongolia; similar facilities are to be granted to Japan in the development of special resources at other places. The so-called co-operation in the management of communications in China covers aviation facilities throughout China and the railway centres in North China, including the Lunghai Line, as well as coastal navigation and along the Yangtse and other communication facilities in North China and along the Lower Yangtse.
All this means that Japan desires to seize all that China possesses, including the control of everything that is necessary for the maintenance of the livelihood of our fellow countrymen, thereby placing them under absolute slavery.
Lest these measures should be incomplete, it was noted in the "remarks" column that a close discussion should be held with the Japanese authorities. In addition, the measures contain detailed provisions concerning the relations between the puppet Central Government on the one hand and the "Reformed Government" in Nanking, the Provisional Government in North China and the Mongolian Government on the other. The principal object of these measures is to facilitate the gradual disintegration of Chinese territory. What has attracted the close attention of the people are the paragraphs referring individually to Amoy and Hainan Island. According to these paragraphs, Amoy is to be converted into a special administrative area, while, on the other hand, Japan is to be recognized as having special rights to deal with aviation, navigation and communication facilities on the island, to develop and utilize all the special resources of the island for national defence purposes. This is tantamount to the perpetual cession of these two places to Japan.
The paragraphs also refer to certain specially designated isles along the South China coast. We should realize that all this means that Japan intends to use China to finance her adventures in the north and the south.
A study of this secret pact reveals the fact that it is far more poisonous and comprehensive than the Twenty-One Demands that were submitted to the late Yuan Shih-kai by Japan in the 4th Year (1915) of the Chinese Republic. If these humiliating terms are accepted, China will be plunged into a hopeless state, while the 450,000,000 descendants of Emperor Huang Tih will have no more hope for survival and East Asia and the world will be faced with a great calamity.
Yet Wang Ching-wei, a heartless person, gladly signed this pact on December 30 last year.
Fellow countrymen, does this pact mean peace or is it one that has sold the nation? Is it a pact that will lead to a readjustment of diplomatic relations between the two countries or is it one that contains terms humiliating to the nation? Will the enforcement of the terms stipulated in this pact assure the independence and freedom of China or will it lead to the complete deprivation of China's independence and freedom?

(10) 关于中国资源开发、海关关税、航空、交通及气象等事项，将达成一项完全符合日本要求的协定。
(11) 在资源开发与利用方面，日本将在华北及内蒙古享有特殊便利；在其他地方开发特种资源时，亦将给予日本类似的便利。所谓在中国交通管理方面的合作，涵盖全中国的航空设施、包括陇海线在内的华北铁路枢纽，以及沿海航运、长江沿线和华中其他交通设施，以及华北和长江下游的交通设施。
这一切意味着日本企图攫取中国所有的一切，包括控制维持我国同胞生计所必需的一切，从而将他们置于绝对的奴役之下。
唯恐这些措施尚不完备，在“备注”栏中指出，应与日本当局进行密切商讨。此外，这些措施还包含关于伪中央政府对一方面与南京“维新政府”、华北“临时政府”及蒙古政府另一方面之间关系的详细规定。这些措施的主要目的是便于逐步分裂中国领土。引起民众密切关注的是分别提及厦门和海南岛的条款。根据这些条款，厦门将被改为特别行政区，而另一方面，日本在该岛的航空、航海及交通设施方面的特殊权利将得到承认，并为国防目的开发和利用该岛的所有特种资源。这无异于将这两个地方永久割让给日本。
这些条款还提及华南沿海某些特别指定的岛屿。我们应该认识到，这一切意味着日本打算利用中国来为其在北方和南方的冒险行动提供资金。
研究这项秘密协定 reveals the fact that it is far more poisonous and comprehensive than the Twenty-One Demands that were submitted to the late Yuan Shih-kai by Japan in the 4th Year (1915) of the Chinese Republic.（注：此处原文为英文混合，依要求保留或翻译，鉴于上下文连贯性，译为：这项秘密协定的研究表明，其毒害性和全面性远超日本于中华民国四年（1915年）向已故袁世凯提出的“二十一条”。）如果接受这些屈辱条款，中国将陷入绝望的境地，而黄帝子孙四亿五千万人将再无生存希望，东亚乃至世界将面临巨大的灾难。
然而，无情之徒汪精卫竟于去年12月30日欣然签署了这项协定。
同胞们，这项协定意味着和平，还是卖国？它是导致两国关系调整的协定，还是包含辱国条款的协定？执行这项协定规定的条款是保障中国的独立自由，还是导致中国独立自由的彻底丧失？

January 22, 1940.

Chinese-American Daily News, Ta Mei Pao, National Herald,
Hwa Pao, Shun Pao and Sin Wan Pao (Hongkong telegram):-

TWO CLOSE FOLLOWERS OF WANG CHING-WEI DESERT CLIQUE :
AGREEMENT SIGNED BY WANG WITH JAPANESE AUTHORITIES DISCLOSED

Kao Chung-woo (高宗武) and Tao Hsi-sun(陶希聖)
are two close followers of Wang Ching-wei. Owing to a
conflict of opinion with Wang, they left Shanghai recently
and are now in Hongkong. (Translator's note:- Kao Chung-
woo is the Foreign Minister-Elect of the proposed new
National Government at Nanking; Tao Hsi-sun is the Chief of
the Central Publicity Bureau of the orthodox Kuomintang.)
The agreement signed between Wang Ching-wei
and the Japanese authorities on December 30, 1939, has now
been published by the "Ta Kung Pao" (大公報) at Hongkong.
It contains the following 13 conditions :-
(1) That Manchukuo be recognized.
(2) That co-operation, especially in the economic field,
be effected with Japan and Manchukuo.
(3) That an Anti-Communist International Joint Front be
formed.
(4) That North China and Inner Mongolia be marked out as
special zones.
(5) That Japan be allowed to retain her favourable economic
situation along the Lower Yangtze Valley.
(6) That Japan be allowed to retain her special position
at Amoy and on Hainan Island.
(7) That Japan be recognized as having the right to station
her naval and military units in North China and Inner
Mongolia, and at certain designated places along the
Yangtze as well as at various islands along the coast
in South China.
(8) That Japan be recognized as having the right to supervise
railways, aviation, postal administration, important
harbours and water highways throughout China.
(9) That the strength of Chinese soldiers and policemen in
certain areas be reduced.
(10) That the losses sustained by Japanese civilians residing
in China prior to the hostilities be made good.
(11) That special agreements be signed with Japan to develop
production, to promote trading, to raise the Customs
tariff and to give Japan special privileges in these
matters.
(12) That the new Chinese Government engage Japanese advisors.
(13) That an Autonomous Political Committee be established
in North China to direct administrative affairs.
As China could hardly accept these conditions,
Kao Chung-woo and Tao Hsi-sun left Shanghai. Upon their
arrival in Hongkong, they sent a joint telegram to Wang
Ching-wei asking him to repent and not to be utilized by
Japan.----- Havas.

汪精卫两名亲信脱离派系：
汪与日本当局签署的协定被披露

高宗武 (Kao Chung-woo) 和陶希圣 (Tao Hsi-sun)
是汪精卫的两名亲信。由于与汪意见不合，他们最近离开上海，
现居香港。（译者注：高宗武是拟议中的南京新
国民政府的外交部长候任人选；陶希圣是正统国民党
中央宣传部部长。）
汪精卫与日本当局于1939年12月30日签署的协定，
现已由香港的《大公报》公布。
其中包含以下13项条件：
(1) 承认满洲国。
(2) 与日本及满洲国实行合作，特别是在经济领域。
(3) 组建反共国际联合战线。
(4) 将华北和内蒙古划为特区。
(5) 允许日本保持在长江下游地区的有利经济地位。
(6) 允许日本保持在厦门和海南岛的特殊地位。
(7) 承认日本有权在华北和内蒙古、长江沿线某些指定地点
以及华南沿海各岛屿驻扎海军和军事单位。
(8) 承认日本有权监督全中国的铁路、航空、邮政管理、重要
港口和水路。
(9) 减少某些地区的中国士兵和警察人数。
(10) 赔偿战前居住在中国的日本平民遭受的损失。
(11) 与日本签订特别协定，以发展生产、促进贸易、提高海关关税
并在这些事项上给予日本特权。
(12) 新中国政府聘请日本顾问。
(13) 在华北设立自治政治委员会以指导行政事务。
由于中国几乎无法接受这些条件，
高宗武和陶希圣离开了上海。抵达香港后，他们
联名致电汪精卫，劝其悔悟，不要被日本利用。----- 哈瓦斯社。

The report published in the Ta Mei Pao of
January 14, 1940 to the effect that Chen Kung-poh
(陳公博), Kao Chung-wu (高宗武) and Tao Hsi-sen
(陶希聖) have severed their connections with
Wang's regime and left Shanghai for Hongkong several
days ago, is true.

Chen Kung Poh was a close follower of Wang
Ching Wei who is said to have rated him higher than
Chow Fu-hai and Chu Ming Nyi. When the Kuomintang
formed by Wang Ching Wei convened a conference in
Yu Yuen Road in latter August, 1939, Wang sent a
telegram to Chen asking him to come to Shanghai.
Chen came to Shanghai about the end of November, 1939,
after Wang had undertaken to guarantee his absolute
freedom of movement. Discussions between Wang
and Chen, however, failed to bring about an agreement
for cooperation because Chen, although he approved
of Wang's peace movement, strongly opposed Wang's
proposals for Sino-Japanese rapprochement. Seeing
that Wang would not be likely to adopt his views, he
abruptly left Shanghai for Hongkong about the middle
of December, 1939.

Tao Hsi-sen was formerly the chief of the
Literature and Arts Research Section of the Military
Affairs Commission of the National Government which
is engaged in the compilation of propaganda literature
and the production of pro-National Government films.

Made by D.S.I. Lian Chung Chien Forwarded by D. I. Crawford

In the evening of January 10, 1940, copies of
a pamphlet entitled "An open letter to various
circles on the reasons for the delay in the formation
of the Central Government" were distributed in various
streets in the Western District, O.C.L.. The
pamphlet is undated and does not mention its origin
but there is no doubt that it was issued by Wang
Ching Wei's party. A translation of the pamphlet,
a copy of which has been obtained and is attached
hereto, reads as follows:-
"It was at first rumoured that the Central
Government was to be formed on October 10, 1939,
later it was said the formation was postponed
till November 12, 1939 and subsequently it was
alleged that it was certain that the administration
would be inaugurated on January 1, 1940.
However, these dates passed by one after the
other, but the government still remains in the
paper stage and many have begun to doubt if the
organization would come into existence at all.
"In connection with the situation, Chow Fu
Hai (周佛海), a member of the Central Executive
Committee of this party (? Wang Ching Wei's Kuo-
mintang), wrote an article entitled "The organization
of the Central Government" (關於組織中央政府)
in which he gave a detailed account of the stand

the belief that the Central Government will be
eventually inaugurated."
Inquiries show that about a week ago, members
of Wang Ching Wei's party were jubilant over the
imminent inauguration of the Central Government.
However, the reports carried in the press during the
past few days regarding the inevitable fall of the
Japanese Cabinet, Wang Ching Wei's supporter, has
again dispelled their hopes with the result that they
became discouraged and despondent. The pamphlets,
which form the subject of this report, were apparently
issued to comfort and pacify these members.

According to information just received by the
Shanghai Branch of the Asia Development Board from Tokyo
Headquarters, agreement has been reached between the
representatives of the Chinese Government of Wang Ching
Wei, now in a state of formation, and the China Board by
which the Government would base its future policy on three
principles of the late Dr. Sun Yat Sen and would retain
the Kuomintang flag as the national flag. Leaders of the
new Government consider themselves to be the representatives
of the Orthodox Kuomintang, whereas the members of the
Nationalist Government in Chungking are regarded by them
as bogus representatives.

Information is also on hand to the effect that no
civilian population would be permitted to return to certain
areas of Nantao which would be set aside as a Japanese
Military Area. Works would soon begin at the Chinese
Arsenal for its improvement and enlargement as well as at
the Kiangnan Dock which would be greatly enlarged so as to
be able to carry on any repairs to the Japanese Navy.

Since the inauguration of the Wang Ching Wei
Government, Chapei would be opened for the civil population
for which purpose several Sino-Japanese Realty Companies
are at present building numerous blocks of houses in Chapei
rents for which would be extremely low. By this measure it
is proposed to attract the Chinese population from the
Settlement and French Concession to settle in Chapei and "
to compensate " to a certain extent former residents of
Nantao.

Maklansky

CHINA PRESS.

DEC 2 - 1939

Japanese And
Wang Agree On
China Policy

A basic program of economic co-operation between the Japanese government, and Wang Ching-wei proposed head of the new "Central China" puppet regime, has been agreed to, declared the Japanese Embassy spokesman at a press interview here yesterday afternoon.

The Japanese have agreed that Wang must establish a firm and independent government and Wang has agreed that the Japanese must not withdraw their troops from China, the spokesman said.

Delays in the matter of setting up the new Nanking regime were explained by the spokesman as being due to the necessity for ironing out matters of detail. The spokesman brought forward as an example the post Revolutionary War period in the United States when the infant republic had heavy sledding in setting up governmental machinery.

In the same category, he said, is the formation of the new Chinese regime. He failed to point out, however, that the American republic was built through its own efforts against the desire of the rest of the world, whereas the puppet regime of Central China will have the help of a great power.

Asked whether any response had been received to Wang's recent radio appeal for military desertions from the National Government to his own cause, another spokesman said there had been reaction but the matter was very delicate. He averred the adherence of a certain General Feng to Wang's colors, along with 20,000 troops. But he was unable to disclose the area of this officer's operations except to say that he was campaigning "with the Japanese army's permission" outside the occupied territories.

1939年12月2日

日本与汪精卫就
对华政策达成一致

日本大使馆发言人在昨日下午的新闻采访中表示，日本政府与拟任新“华中”傀儡政权首脑的汪精卫之间，已就一项经济合作的基本方案达成一致。

该发言人称，日方已同意汪精卫必须建立一个稳固且独立的政府，而汪精卫也已同意日军不得从中国撤军。

关于组建新的南京政权事宜的延误，发言人解释称，这是由于需要解决细节问题所致。发言人举出美国革命战争后的时期为例，当时这个新生的共和国在建立政府机制方面步履维艰。

他说，中国新政权的组建也属于同一类情况。然而，他未能指出的是，美利坚共和国是违背世界其他国家的意愿、依靠自身努力建立的，而华中傀儡政权则将得到一个强国的帮助。

当被问及是否收到对汪精卫最近通过广播呼吁国民政府军人倒戈投靠其阵营的任何回应时，另一位发言人表示虽有反应，但此事非常微妙。他断言某位冯将军已率两万部队投奔汪精卫麾下。但他无法透露该军官的活动区域，仅称其是在“经日军许可”的情况下，在占领区以外进行活动。

Date December 1 1939.

Subject. Pessimism among Waung Ching Wei's Clique over its future plans.
Made by/ ____ and. ____ Forwarded by Supt. Tan Shao Liang 4/6/44
O.T.

（批：yfw Roberts）

According to information furnished by a follower of Waung Ching Wei, the future plans for the formation of a central government are not very hopeful due to the lack of support furnished by the Japanese. The latter at present seem to be entertaining some doubt as to whether Waung Ching Wei would be able to bring about the surrender of the more important Chungking officials to his cause as was promised before taking up the peace movement and to talk peace with Chiang Kai Shek after his government has been formed.

Japanese politicians in Tokio, it is reported, hold divergent views regarding the support to be given to Waung Ching Wei. Premier Abe and his followers prefer an immediate cessation of hostilities with Chungking in order to avoid further sacrifices on Japan part and allow her to expand her trade with foreign countries by taking advantage of the European war. It will be almost impossible for Waung Ching Wei to attain this object even if his government is formed and recognized by Japan, because this step will increase the hostility of Chiang Kai Shek, who will never countenance such conditions and will not discuss peace with Waung Ching Wei. Furthermore Waung Ching Wei has made certain demands for independence in financial and military administrations which are considered by the Japanese as unreasonable, excessive and unacceptable in as much as Waung's influence and power has been procured through Japanese support.

CONFIDENTIAL
t. S. C G

（印：SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL COMMISSIONER'S OFFICE * 2 - DEC. 1939 * B）

由/ ____ 和. ____ 制作，由谭绍良警司转呈 4/6/44
O.T.

（批注：yfw Roberts）

根据一名汪精卫追随者提供的信息，由于缺乏日本方面的支持，组建中央政府的未来计划前景并不乐观。后者目前似乎对汪精卫能否如发起和平运动前所承诺的那样，促使重庆方面更重要的官员向其阵营投降，并在其政府成立后与蒋介石进行和谈，持怀疑态度。

据报道，东京的日本政客们在给予汪精卫何种支持的问题上持有不同观点。首相阿部及其追随者倾向于立即停止与重庆方面的敌对行动，以避免日本方面进一步牺牲，并利用欧洲战争的机会扩大与外国的贸易。即使汪精卫的政府成立并获得日本承认，他也几乎不可能实现这一目标，因为此举将加剧蒋介石的敌意，蒋绝不会容忍此类条件，也不会与汪精卫讨论和平。此外，汪精卫提出了在财政和军事行政方面独立的要求，日本人认为这些要求不合理、过分且不可接受，因为汪的影响力和权力是通过日本的支持获得的。

t. S. C G

page_data.en:
DAILY NEWS.
NOV 25 1938

Chungking Awaits
Wang Move

Change of Stand Over So-
Called Peace Move Seen
As Most Significant

Chungking, Nov. 24.
Chungking circles hesitate to ex-
press an opinion on the article
published yesterday in the "Central
China Daily News," mouth-piece of
Mr. Wang Ching-wei, as the details
and circumstances leading to its
publication are not known.
The article, "which naturally came
as a surprise," gives a somewhat
different standpoint from that of Gen-
eral Nobuyuki Abe, Japanese Premier,
regarding the so-called new "Central
Government of China" and Sino-
Japanese relations.
There is much speculation here as
to the motive behind Mr. Wang
Ching-wei's latest stand.
One of the prevailing views sug-
gests that the article was written at
the suggestion of Tokyo, "in order to
strengthen their stand against ex-
cessive demands by the Japanese
army."
Other quarters say that Mr. Wang
Ching-wei may have published the
article for internal consumption "in
an attempt to create a favourable im-
pression among the Chinese people."
The opinion is also expressed that
"there is always the possibility that
Mr. Wang Ching-wei is becoming fed-
up with excessive Japanese demands,
which would make it very difficult
for him to establish a régime with any
chance of being accepted by the Chi-
nese public."
Informed circles here are therefore
awaiting further developments with
considerable interest, but they all
agree that the establishment of the
new "Central Government" will prob-
ably be delayed for some time.—
Reuter.

The Article

Holding that the Chungking Gov-
ernment "has been reduced to a local
regime because of its depending on
Russia, Great Britain and the United
States," the article in the "Central
China Daily News" said that "whether
the central government may induce
members of the Chungking Govern-
ment to join it, depends entirely upon
the soundness of the bases of the new
administration."
The newspaper emphasized that
"the central government cannot be
reorganized by Japan, nor can Chiang
Kai-shek's administration be over-
thrown by Japan."

It is stressed that the redevelop-
ment of a Chinese government not
under Gen. Chiang is a matter entire-
ly for the Chinese.
Questioned at the Japanese press
conference yesterday regarding the
Japanese attitude to a recent leading
article in Mr. Wang Ching-wei's
"Central China Daily News," the
Japanese Embassy spokesman said
that inasmuch as it was based on a
statement made by Gen. Abe, the
general view expressed was fully
acceptable to the Japanese Govern-
ment. Mr. Wang showed clearly that
he is establishing a central govern-
ment, not under Japanese pressure,
but one in which he thinks lies the
salvation of China.
Mr. Wang fully pointed out that
there can be no discussion of the
evacuation of Japanese troops from
China until peace and order had been
established—if peace, then the troops
would be withdrawn.
It was further observed that should
a Wang government be set up, it
would have no army of its own to
maintain peace and order in the ter-
ritory under its control. The Japan-
ese Government at no time, continued
the spokesman, had entertained the
idea of permanent garrisons in China.
Gen. Abe had stated that his govern-
ment had no desire to dictate to a
new Chinese government—advice
would be given, if desired.
Anyone could observe with the
large number of Japanese troops in
China, that Japan could dictate, but
people could by actual conditions note
that such was not the intention of the
Japanese Government.
The spokesman adduced that cer-
tain foreign papers had commented
editorially that the Japanese Govern-
ment did not trust Mr. Wang Ching-
wei and had no confidence in him.
That the Japanese had full confidence
in him was to be seen in the fact that
last week, when Mr. Suma, spokes-
man of the Gaimusho, called on Mr.
Wang, he brought personal messages
from Prince Konoye, Gen. Abe and
Gen. Hata. These should suffice to
dispel any baseless conjectures.
Mr. Wang's editorial, the spokesman
concluded, indicated that the time
element did not enter into the scheme
of things. There might be delays,
but he wanted a good government,
the best possible for the people of
China.
page_data.zh:
《每日新闻》。
1938年11月25日

重庆等待
汪精卫的举动

所谓和平运动立场的转变
被视为最具重大意义

重庆，11月24日电。
鉴于昨日发表在汪精卫先生喉舌《华中日报》上的文章，其发表细节及背景情况尚不为人知，重庆方面对表达意见持犹豫态度。
这篇文章“自然令人感到意外”，就所谓新的“中华民国中央政府”及中日关系而言，其立场与日本首相阿部信行将军的立场略有不同。
此处对于汪精卫先生最新立场背后的动机有很多猜测。
一种普遍的观点认为，该文章是应东京方面的建议而写，“旨在加强他们对抗日本军队过度要求的立场”。
其他方面则表示，汪精卫先生发表该文章可能是为了“内部消化”，即“试图在中国民众中创造良好的印象”。
也有观点认为，“汪精卫先生有可能对日本的过度要求感到厌倦，这将使他很难建立一个有机会被中国公众接受的政权”。
因此，此间知情各界正怀着极大兴趣等待事态的进一步发展，但大家一致认为，新“中央政府”的建立可能会推迟一段时间。——路透社。

该文章

《华中日报》的文章认为，重庆政府“因依赖俄国、英国和美国而已降格为地方政权”，并称“中央政府能否促使重庆政府成员加入，完全取决于新行政当局基础的稳固程度”。
该报强调，“中央政府不能由日本重组，蒋介石的行政当局也不能由日本推翻”。

文章强调，重建一个不在蒋将军领导下的中国政府，完全是中国人自己的事情。
在昨日的日本记者招待会上，当被问及日本政府对汪精卫先生《华中日报》最近一篇社论的态度时，日本大使馆发言人表示，鉴于该社论基于阿部将军的声明，其所表达的总体观点完全为日本政府所接受。汪先生清楚地表明，他正在建立一个中央政府，这不是在日本压力下建立的，而是他认为能拯救中国的政府。
汪先生充分指出，在和平与秩序建立之前，无法讨论日军从中国撤军的问题——如果有和平，军队就会撤离。
此外还指出，如果成立汪氏政府，它将没有自己的军队来维持其控制领土内的和平与秩序。发言人继续说，日本政府从未有过在中国永久驻军的想法。阿部将军曾表示，他的政府无意向新的中国政府发号施令——如果需要，会提供建议。
任何人都可以观察到，鉴于在华日军数量庞大，日本本可以发号施令，但人们可以通过实际情况注意到，这并非日本政府的意图。
发言人援引某些外国报纸的社论评论称，日本政府不信任汪精卫先生，对他没有信心。日本人对他充满信心的事实体现在：上周，外务省发言人须磨弥吉郎先生拜访汪先生时，带来了近卫公爵、阿部将军和畑俊六将军的个人口信。这些足以消除任何毫无根据的猜测。
发言人总结道，汪先生的社论表明，时间因素并未纳入计划之中。可能会有延误，但他想要一个好的政府，即尽可能适合中国人民的政府。

New Governments to

Peiping, Oct 19.

新政府将于
10月28日会晤

北平，10月19日。
据此处昨日预示，在10月28日于青岛开始的第七次会议上，“维新”和“临时”中国政府联合委员会将投票赞成解散，以利于拟议中的中央政治委员会。
新委员会将由“维新”国民党主席汪精卫先生于11月组建。
预计会议将决定“维新”和“临时”政府参加中央政治委员会的代表人选，并调整基本行政政策，这可能是解散前的最后一次会议。——同盟社。

SHANGHAI TIMES.

OCT 24 1939

Conference
With Wang
Ching-wei

Gen. Itagaki's Journey
To Shanghai Includes
Talk With Wang

TOKYO, Oct. 23.—Lieut.-General
Seishiro Itagaki, Chief of Staff of
the Japanese Expeditionary Forces
to China and former War Minister,
who is in Shanghai on an inspec-
tion tour, had an important talk
with Mr. Wang Ching-wei, leader
of the new Kuomintang, at Shang-
hai on Friday evening, it was learnt
here to-day.

Lieut.-General Itagaki was accom-
panied by Lieut.-General Seiichi
Kita, Director of the North China
liaison office of the Asia Develop-
ment Board.

Mr. Wang and Lieut.-General
Itagaki were said to have exchang-
ed opinions regarding the formation
of a Central Political Council
which is expected to be a nucleus
for the projected new Central
Government in China.

The meeting was attended by Mr.
Chou Fo-hai, leading supporter of
Mr. Wang's peace movement, who
returned to Shanghai recently
after a visit in Tokyo.

It was learnt that Mr. Wang
met a group of 20 Japanese Army
and Navy officers and officials of
the Asia Development Board on
Saturday.—Domei.

1939年10月24日

与汪精卫的会谈
板垣将军之行
抵沪包括与汪会谈

东京，10月23日电。——据本日在此间获悉，日本中国派遣军参谋长、前陆军大臣板垣征四郎中将正在上海进行视察，于周五晚在上海与新民党（新国民党）领袖汪精卫先生进行了重要会谈。

板垣中将由亚洲开发协会华北联络局局长北一哉少将陪同。

据悉，汪先生与板垣中将就成立中央政治委员会交换了意见，该委员会预计将成为拟议中的中国新中央政府的核心。

出席会议的还有汪先生和平运动的主要支持者周佛海先生，他近期访问东京后返回上海。

另悉，汪先生于周六会见了一组20名日本陆海军军官及亚洲开发协会的官员。——同盟社。

（批注：6 3/10）

page_data.en:
MAINICHI 23.10.39 (PM)

"GENERAL ITAGAKI, WANG CHING WEI AND GENERAL KITA
HOLD CONFERENCE IN SHANGHAI AND REACH
COMPLETE AGREEMENT

Lieutenant-General Itagaki,
Chief of the General Staff to the Japanese Expeditionary
Forces in China, arrived at Shanghai on the afternoon
of October 19 to inspect the situation in the areas under
his command. At 8 p.m. October 22, General Itagaki
together with General Kita, Chief of the Asia Development
Board in North China, General Kusumoto, Deputy Chief
of the Asia Development Board in Central China, held a
conference with Wang Ching Wei, Chairman of the Central
Executive Committee of the China Kuomintang, his Secretary
Tsu Min Yee and Chow Fu Hai at a certain place in Shanghai.

The conference lasted about three hours. Mr. Wang
Ching Wei had a conference on Far Eastern affairs with
General Itagaki in Tokyo in June when the latter was
War Minister.

The nature of the conference
in Shanghai has not been disclosed, but it is believed
that the question of the early calling of a meeting
of the Central Political Council and the establishment
of a Central Government were considered. Furthermore,
it would appear as if General Itagaki and Wang Ching
Wei have reached a complete agreement at their exchange
of views.
page_data.zh:
《每日新闻》 1939.10.23 (下午版)

“板垣将军、汪精卫与北将军
在上海举行会议并达成
完全一致

日本中国派遣军总参谋长板垣中将，于10月19日下午抵达上海，视察其管辖区域的情况。10月22日晚8时，板垣将军会同亚洲开发协会华北局长北将军、华中副局长楠本将军，在上海某地与中华民国国民党中央执行委员会主席汪精卫、其秘书褚民谊及周佛海举行了会议。

会议持续约三小时。汪精卫先生曾于今年6月在东京与时任陆军大臣的板垣将军就远东事务进行过会谈。

上海会议的性质尚未披露，但据信，会议审议了尽早召开中央政治委员会会议及建立中央政府的问题。此外，板垣将军与汪精卫在交换意见后似乎已达成完全一致。

elements to the effect that during his last visit to
Tokio before he took up the mission of bringing about the
establishment of a central regime, Waung Ching Wei was
promised strong support by the Japanese Government.
Since his arrival in Shanghai, he discovered that he
was confronted with opposition from many rival parties.
whilst his work in connection with the organization

such as the Sin Min Hui (新民會) in the North, the

(梁鴻志), the second organization and the third is

published by the last named party called the "Chen Chi"
(正氣) openly attacked Waung Ching Wei in the peace
talks and in bringing about the revival of the new
Kuomintang Party.

During the last conference at Nanking between
the three prominent heads, Waung Ching Wei, Wong Keh Min
and Liang Hung Tse, nothing of a satisfactory nature was
agreed upon, Wong and Liang having recommended their
followers to become two-thirds of the Cabinet members.

参照1939年10月6日的报告，收到进一步情报称，汪精卫及其手下促成浙江“独立”的努力已告失败。看来，浙江省主席黄绍竑将军并未完全控制所有部队，大多数来自江西的军官直接受重庆中央政府监管，在目前情况下不太可能被诱降。

虽然此情报来自汪精卫的敌对派系（亲日派），但似乎相当可靠。

据报道，本月月初，日本海军恢复了在温州附近浙江沿海的封锁活动，这加强了人们认为日本已放弃与当地当局达成妥协的所有希望的信念。

- - - - - -

DELAY IN FORMING THE "CENTRAL GOVERNMENT" BY
WAUNG CHING WEI
CAUSED BY ALLEGED LACK OF SUPPORT FROM DIFFERENT
CIRCLES.
SENSATIONAL DEVELOPMENTS PREDICTED.

With reference to previous reports on the subject of
Waung Ching Wei and his followers contemplating the formation
of a Central Government to unify control of areas under Japanese
occupation, information has been received from pro-Japanese
elements on good authority, that there are still many obstacles
to the path in the formation of the Government. Before taking
up this important position, Waung is exercising great care in
choosing the right locality for the seat of the Government and
the people who promise him support. He does not prefer Peiping
nor Nanking nor Canton, owing to the unfavourable surroundings
and the deep rooted influence of the old fashioned officials.
During his last visit to Canton he evidently failed to bring
over General Chang Fah Kwei ( 張發奎 ) to his side, and
he has now realized that to make his policy a success he has
to establish his own influence which means he should have a
military strength of his own, independent from Peiping or
Nanking. Endeavours, it is reported, have been and are being
made to induce General Hwang Shao Hsiung ( 黃紹 ), Chairman
of the Chekiang Provincial Government, who has under his
command 300,000 men in the province to join Waung in the "peace"
movement. This done, Waung Ching Wei will make Ching-hwa
( 金華 ), Chekiang, the capital of the new Government.
General Hwang, it is known, was formerly attached to Waung's
clique, but it is premature to state whether Hwang is able to

汪精卫组建“中央政府”的延误
据称是由于缺乏各界支持。
预测将有轰动性发展。

关于此前有关汪精卫及其追随者 contemplate 组建中央政府以统一控制日占区的报告，从可靠的亲日分子处收到情报称，在组建政府的道路上仍存在许多障碍。在担任这一重要职位之前，汪在选择政府所在地和承诺支持他的人选方面极为谨慎。由于环境不利以及旧式官员根深蒂固的影响，他既不喜欢北平，也不喜欢南京或广州。在他最近访问广州期间，显然未能争取到张发奎将军站在他的一边，他现在意识到，要使他的政策成功，必须建立自己的影响力，这意味着他应该拥有独立于北平或南京的军事力量。据报道，过去和现在都在努力诱使浙江省政府主席、在该省统率30万军队的黄绍竑将军加入汪的“和平”运动。如果做到这一点，汪精卫将使浙江金华成为新政府的首都。众所周知，黄将军以前依附于汪的派系，但现在断言黄是否能够

bring all his subordinates over without encountering serious
difficulties. Waung expects to receive a definite reply
in the middle of October or beginning of November. Without
this support waung will be confronted with opposition from
many rivals and his plans may come to a failure; although
he is strongly backed up by the Japanese Army, (not Navy).

Politically, Waung Ching Wei is not liked by members
of the Peiping and Nanking Governments and besides, he is
strongly criticised by Chen Chung Fu ( 陳中孚 ) and
Hu Shih Cheng, ( 〔此处转录不清〕 ), another pro-Japanese faction
of some influence.

As indicated above his success or failure depends
entirely on the attitude of the Chekiang authorities.

REPORT
Date September 21 1939

Subject Reported peace talks advocated by Wang Ching Wei's Clique.

Made by. and Forwarded by Supt. Tan Shao Liang

According to information from a close
follower of Wang Ching Wei, secret negotiations
have been exchanged between Wang Ching Wei and dele-
gates of T.V.Soong and H.H.Kung in Shanghai as to
terms for a possible conclusion of peace between
China and Japan. The names of the two important
Chungking delegates were not divulged but it is alleged
they acted on full authority from Generalissimo
Chiang Kai Shek. According to the informant, although
Japan does not wish to negotiate with Chungking Govern-
ment direct, she does not object to Mr. Wang undertaking
the negotiations. Japan, it is alleged, is willing
to withdraw her troops from South China when she is
sure that the Chinese troops replacing them are pro-
Japanese. The most serious obstacles to the negotia-
tions would appear to be the demand for the resignation
of Chiang Kai Shek and several other Chungking officials
noted for their anti-Japanese attitude and the disband-
ment of Chinese soldiers especially communist troops
whose leaders are hostile to Japanese.

It is alleged by pro-Japanese elements that
before long, Lung Yuen, the Governor of Yunnan, will annou-
nce his sympathy with the peace movement and if this is
followed by other Chungking Generals in Kwangtung and
Kwangsi, there will be no alternative for the Chinese
Government but to surrender.

The above information, however, lacks confirma-
tion from Chinese ex-government officials.

D. C. (Special branch)
Superintendent.
（签名：Tan Shaoliang）

撰写人及转呈人 谭绍良警司

根据汪精卫一名亲信提供的消息，汪精卫与宋子文和孔祥熙在上海的代表之间已就中日可能达成和平的条款进行了秘密谈判。两名重要的重庆代表姓名未予透露，但据称他们是奉蒋介石委员长的全权授权行事。据线人称，虽然日本不希望直接与重庆政府谈判，但并不反对由汪先生进行谈判。据称，一旦日本确信接替其军队的中国军队是亲日的，便愿意从华南撤军。谈判面临的最严重障碍似乎是要求蒋介石及其他几位以反日态度著称的重庆官员辞职，以及解散中国军队，特别是那些领导人敌视日本的共产党部队。

亲日分子声称，不久之后，云南省主席龙云将宣布同情和平运动，如果广东和广西的其他重庆将领也效仿此举，中国政府将别无选择，只能投降。

然而，上述信息缺乏来自中国前政府官员的证实。

CONFIDENTIAL
SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE.
File No. 8986 (c)
S.1, Special Branch: Shanghai,
REPORT
Date September 12, 1939.
Subject. Wang Ching Wei - proposed formation of a central
Government at Nanking.
Made by C.D.I. Sih Tse Liang Forwarded by R. W. Mac Calie D.S.P.

Wang Ching Wei is still planning the
formation of a central government at Nanking with
himself as the President. If he can succeed in
persuading the Provisional Government at Peiping
and the Reformed Government at Nanking to yield to
his proposal, he expects to effect the amalgamation
of the two Governments before the end of 1939 into
a central government to be inaugurated at Nanking
on January 1, 1940. The new central government
will abolish the five barred flag and adopt the
"white sun and blue sky" emblem.

It is further reported that in the new
government Wang Ching Wei will content himself with
the position of Chairman of the Executive Yuan in
case he cannot obtain the position of President.
If so, Tong Kuh Ming (王克敏), head of the
Provisional Government, will be made the President
of the new government. The Chairmen of various
Yuans of the Reformed Government will be appointed
vice-chairmen of the same Yuans in the new govern-
ment while the positions of Chairmen will be left
unfilled in order to persuade those in similar
positions in the National Government at Chungking
to take them up. Chow Fu Hai (周佛海), ardent
follower of Wang Ching Wei, will be made vice-
chairman of the Military Affairs Commission of the
new government.

主题。汪精卫 - 拟在南京组建中央政府。
撰写人 C.D.I. Sih Tse Liang 转呈人 R. W. Mac Calie 副警务处长。

汪精卫仍在策划在南京组建中央政府，并由他本人担任总统。如果他能够说服北平的临时政府和南京的维新政府接受他的提议，他预计将在1939年底前将两个政府合并为一个中央政府，并于1940年1月1日在南京正式成立。新中央政府将废除五色旗，采用“青天白日”徽记。

另有报道称，在新政府中，如果汪精卫无法获得总统职位，他将满足于担任行政院院长一职。如果是这样，临时政府首脑王克敏 (Tong Kuh Ming) 将被任命为新政府的总统。维新政府各院院长将被任命为新政府相应院的副院长，而院长职位则留空，以便劝说重庆国民政府中担任类似职位的人来就职。汪精卫的狂热追随者周佛海 (Chow Fu Hai) 将被任命为新政府军事委员会的副委员长。
